label: rem:standard-part-classical-limit
title: Standard-part as the exact classical-limit substitute
html:
Example: Jackson derivative

The Jackson derivative

  d_q f(x) = \frac{f(qx) - f(x)}{(q - 1) x}

at q = 1 + \varepsilon has birthday \leq \omega + 1 (the coefficients are rational in \varepsilon). Applying \mathrm{st} recovers the classical derivative exactly:

  \mathrm{st}\!\bigl(d_{1 + \varepsilon} f(x_0)\bigr) = \frac{df}{dx}(x_0)
  \qquad (x_0 \in \mathbb{R}).

This is the exact substitute for the (broken) classical-limit functor (classical limit functor): instead of taking q \to 1 as a topological limit in \mathbb{R}, we evaluate at a specific infinitesimal-shifted surreal and take the standard-part. Unlike the topological limit, this construction makes sense in pure algebra.

Significance for QOU

The main paper's mass formula outputs live in \mathbb{Q}(q) with q = q_0 \in \mathbb{R} as the substrate value. Under a surreal lift, q becomes 1 + \varepsilon and the outputs live in \mathbf{No}_{\mathrm{fin}} (they are rational in \varepsilon). Applying \mathrm{st} recovers exactly the paper's reals; the discarded infinitesimal part is an explicit record of the first-order quantum correction.
